mainTopic: Why פי תקרה יורד וסותם does not save a house breached on two sides, and the dispute between רב and שמואל about an אכסדרה
overview: The עמוד opens by finishing an earlier point: a breach at the corner of a חצר cannot count as a doorway, because nobody builds a doorway in a corner. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's case of a house breached on two sides. It asks why the rule of פי תקרה יורד וסותם does not seal the house, since that rule treats the roof's edge as a wall coming down. The school of רב answers that the breach is at a corner under a slanted roof. שמואל answers that the breach is wider than ten אמות. The גמרא presses שמואל with two questions. It also notes that in the case of an אכסדרה in a valley, שמואל seems to reject the roof-edge rule entirely. That contradiction is resolved: שמואל rejects the rule only when all four sides depend on it, and accepts it for three. The original question is then answered with a corner breach where the roof would have to seal four sides. The גמרא explains why each אמורא did not adopt the other's explanation and lays out the reasons behind their אכסדרה dispute. It gives two opposite versions of whether they argue about openings of ten אמות or wider. A statement of רב יהודה is then introduced, and it continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: A corner breach is not a doorway
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an earlier explanation. The case is a courtyard breached at a corner, and such an opening cannot count as a doorway because people don't build doorways in corners.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the case is where it was breached in a corner, because people do not make a doorway in a corner.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started on the previous עמוד. It explains why this breach in the חצר cancels the wall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A gap of up to ten אמות can usually be treated as a פתח (doorway), and a doorway does not cancel a wall. A gap in a corner, however, looks like a broken wall rather than a doorway, because nobody builds a doorway there. So the gap counts as a real breach.

phrases.english: And the case is where it (the courtyard) was breached in a corner.
phrases.notes: A corner breach opens two sides at once.

phrases.english: For a doorway in a corner
people do not make.
phrases.notes: So the gap cannot be counted as a doorway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes an explanation that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines the case narrowly (a corner breach)
steps.terutzMaskana: A corner opening is never a doorway, so it counts as a breach even if it is ten אמות or less.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: a house breached on two sides
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה: a house breached on two of its sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, a house that was breached on two of its sides.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה. This is a setup line; the question about it comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that a house breached on two sides on שבת may still be carried in for that שבת, but not on a later שבת. Being 'breached on two sides' implies the house now has a real problem. That is what the גמרא will question next.

phrases.english: And likewise, a house that was breached
on two of its sides.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the courtyard case to the house case in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A house breached on two sides is treated as breached; carrying is allowed only for that שבת.

steps.title: Why doesn't the roof's edge seal two sides too?
steps.stepSummary: For a one-side breach we say פי תקרה יורד וסותם, the roof's edge counts as a wall. Why not say the same for two sides?
steps.simpleTranslation: How is this different from a breach on one side, where we say the edge of the roof comes down and closes the gap? For two sides too, let us say the edge of the roof comes down and closes it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It asks why a two-side breach is a problem, when the same roof rule that saves a one-side breach should work here too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of פי תקרה יורד וסותם treats the edge of a roof as if it continues down and forms a wall. That rule should work at every open side of a roofed house. So it seems no breach under a roof should ever cancel the walls.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read מאי שנא as a request for information. It is an attack: the גמרא thinks there should be no difference at all.

phrases.english: How is it different from (a breach on) one side,
where we say:
'The edge of the roof comes down and closes (the gap).'
For two sides too, let us say:
'The edge of the roof comes down and closes (the gap)!'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a house breached on two sides counts as breached
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The roof-edge rule saves a one-side breach and should apply equally at two sides.

steps.title: Answer of רב's school: a corner breach under a slanted roof
steps.stepSummary: The school of רב says the house was breached at a corner and its roof runs diagonally. In that case there is no roof edge to 'come down.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רב said in רב's name: the case is where it was breached in a corner and its roofing is slanted, so we cannot say the edge of the roof comes down and closes.
steps.whatsHappening: The school of רב answers the challenge. It narrows the משנה to a special case in which the roof rule cannot work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The roof rule needs a straight roof edge that looks like the top of a wall. When the roof is slanted or diagonal over a corner breach, there is no such edge. So the rule does not apply, and the house counts as breached.

keyTerms.meaning: the students of רב's academy said

phrases.english: The school of רב said in the name of רב:
The case is where it was breached in a corner
and its roofing is diagonal (slanted),
so that one cannot say
'the edge of the roof comes down and closes.'

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a special case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any house breached on two sides should be saved by the roof's edge.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a corner breach under a slanted roof, where there is no proper roof edge.

steps.title: שמואל's answer: the breach is wider than ten
steps.stepSummary: שמואל answers differently: the משנה refers to a breach wider than ten אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: even more than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives a different answer to the same challenge. In his view, the breach in the משנה is wider than ten אמות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל does not depend on the shape of the roof. He holds that the משנה is talking about a gap wider than ten אמות, which is too wide to count as a doorway (פתח). So it is a real breach that cancels the wall.

phrases.english: And שמואל said:
(It refers) even to (a breach) more than ten (אמות).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to step 3, different from רב's school.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a different special case
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means a breach wider than ten אמות.

steps.title: Challenge to שמואל: then one side should be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the problem is the width, a wide breach on even one side should cancel the walls. So why does the משנה mention two sides?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, (it should be forbidden) even from one side!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's answer. If width is what matters, the משנה's mention of 'two sides' seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under שמואל, the number of breached sides should not matter, because a gap wider than ten cancels the wall on its own. Yet the משנה deliberately says 'two sides.' The answer to this challenge comes next.

phrases.english: If so,
(it should be forbidden) even from one side!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's explanation that the breach is wider than ten
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If width alone is the problem, the משנה's 'two sides' detail is pointless, since one side would be enough.

steps.title: The משנה says two sides because of the house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה mentions two sides only because it also wants to teach the law of a house.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of the house.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 6. According to שמואל, a wide breach on even one side of a חצר is enough to forbid carrying, and the משנה only says 'two sides' for the case of a בית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a חצר, a breach wider than ten אמות on one side already cancels the walls. A בית is different: if it is breached on one side, פי תקרה יורד וסותם fills the gap, so carrying stays permitted. The משנה says 'two sides' so that its statement fits a house as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of the house; the 'two sides' detail is there for the case of a house
A breach or gap in a wall

steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that a חצר needs two breached sides. According to שמואל, one wide breach is enough for a חצר. 'Two sides' is only needed for a בית.

phrases.english: Because of a house.
phrases.notes: That's the whole answer: the 'two sides' wording was chosen because of the house case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by explaining why the משנה says 'two sides.'
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the wording: the משנה's detail is needed for one of its cases (a house), not for all of them.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the משנה said 'two sides,' it seemed that two sides were required in every case, which would not fit שמואל's width explanation.
steps.terutzMaskana: A חצר is forbidden with one wide breach. A בית needs two, because a one-side breach is sealed by the roof edge.

steps.title: The house case itself is now a problem
steps.stepSummary: If the roof edge seals one breached side of a house, why not two breached sides?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the house itself should be difficult: what is different about one side, where we say the edge of the roof comes down and seals? For two sides also, let us say the edge of the roof comes down and seals!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave. If a house survives a one-side breach because of the roof edge, the same reasoning should save it when two sides are breached.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 relied on פי תקרה יורד וסותם to explain why a house needs two breached sides. But the roof edge exists over both breaches, so it should seal both. This brings back the question of step 3, now aimed at שמואל's approach. The answer of רב's school (a corner breach with a diagonal roof) was not part of שמואל's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Should be difficult; let it pose a problem
The edge of the roof is seen as coming down and closing the gap like a wall

steps.confusionAlert: This question repeats the words of step 3 on purpose. The גמרא is not starting over. It is showing that the old question returns against שמואל's approach.

phrases.english: But the house itself should pose a difficulty:
What is different about one side,
where we say the edge of the roof descends and seals?
For two sides as well,
let us say: the edge of the roof descends and seals!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 7 by turning its own logic (the roof edge) against it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 7 that a house is forbidden only with two breached sides, according to שמואל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The roof edge that seals one breach should equally seal a second breach, so there is no reason two sides should differ from one.

steps.title: Does שמואל even accept the roof-edge principle?
steps.stepSummary: A second challenge: in the case of an אכסדרה in a valley, שמואל seems to reject פי תקרה יורד וסותם entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: does שמואל hold that the edge of the roof comes down and seals? But it was stated: about a portico in a valley, רב said one may carry in all of it, and שמואל said one may carry in it only within four אמות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger problem. It quotes a known argument between רב and שמואל which shows that שמואל does not use the roof-edge principle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה is a roof resting on pillars, without real walls. רב permits carrying in all of it because the roof edges count as walls. שמואל allows only four אמות, which means he does not treat the roof edges as walls. If so, the whole explanation of step 7, which relied on the roof edge, seems impossible for שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; introduces an additional challenge
But it was stated (introduces a quoted dispute of אמוראים)
Portico: a roofed structure on pillars, open at the sides
Four cubits: the small area where one may carry in a non-private domain

phrases.english: And furthermore:
Does Shmuel hold
that the edge of the roof descends and seals?
But it was stated:
A portico in a valley:
Rav said: it is permitted to carry in all of it,
phrases.notes: רב holds that the roof edges count as walls.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בָּהּ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת!
phrases.english: One may carry in it only within four cubits!
phrases.notes: This implies that שמואל does not accept the roof-edge principle.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתוּ: מִי אִית לֵיהּ לִשְׁמוּאֵל פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge alongside step 8, this time based on an outside ruling of שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of פי תקרה יורד וסותם within שמואל's explanation (step 7).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל's ruling on the אכסדרה shows he rejects the roof-edge principle, so he cannot rely on it to explain why a house breached on one side is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The dispute between רב and שמואל about an אכסדרה in a valley.

steps.title: שמואל rejects the principle only for four sides
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rejects פי תקרה יורד וסותם only when all four sides depend on it, but accepts it when only three sides do.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult: where he does not hold it, that is with four sides; but with three sides, he does hold it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second challenge from step 9. It limits שמואל's rejection of the roof-edge principle to a structure where all four sides rely on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An אכסדרה in a valley has no real walls at all, so all four sides would be 'walls' made only by the roof edge, and שמואל does not accept that. Where only three sides are formed this way and the fourth is a real wall, שמואל does accept the principle. So his ruling on the אכסדרה does not contradict using the roof edge for a house.

keyTerms.meaning: With four (sides relying on the roof edge)
With three (sides relying on the roof edge)

steps.whatToRemember: According to this answer, שמואל accepts פי תקרה יורד וסותם when it forms three sides, but not when it must form all four, as in an אכסדרה in a valley.

phrases.english: This is not a difficulty:
Where he does not hold it, that is with four sides,
but with three sides, he does hold it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא: כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ בְּאַרְבַּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second challenge (step 9). The first challenge (step 8) is raised again in step 11 and answered in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope: the two rulings of שמואל apply to different cases (four sides compared with three sides).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל's אכסדרה ruling seemed to show that he rejects the roof-edge principle completely.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל rejects the principle only when all four sides depend on it. He accepts it for three sides.

steps.title: The original question still stands
steps.stepSummary: Even after resolving the contradiction in שמואל, the question from step 8 remains: why doesn't פי תקרה יורד וסותם seal two breached sides of a house?
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, it is still difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the question it asked earlier and says it has still not been answered. This line sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9–10 only explained a contradiction between two statements of שמואל. They did not explain why the roof edge cannot seal two breached sides of a house when it can seal one. So the question from step 8 is raised again.

keyTerms.meaning: it is difficult; the question remains

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new question. It is the same question from step 8. The גמרא paused to deal with a side issue in steps 9–10 and is now coming back to it.

phrases.english: In any case, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: We're back to the question from step 8.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side issue of steps 9–10 to the main question of step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading that the משנה forbids a house breached on two sides
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the roof edge can seal one side, it should be able to seal two sides as well.

steps.title: The house was breached at a corner
steps.stepSummary: Following בי רב, the גמרא explains the משנה as a house breached at a corner. For רב the roof is slanted. For שמואל the roofing is arranged so that sealing would have to work on all four sides.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the school of רב said in the name of רב: the case is where the house was breached at a corner, and its roofing was slanted. Here too, for שמואל, the case is where it was breached at a corner, and its roofing is 'in four.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. It says the משנה is not talking about a normal breach, but a special corner breach where the roof cannot seal it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says the roof is slanted, so its edge does not line up straight over the breach and cannot 'come down and seal.' שמואל uses a similar idea: the roof is set up so that פי תקרה would have to seal all four sides. In step 10 we learned שמואל rejects פי תקרה in exactly that situation.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the rule of פי תקרה is not cancelled. It simply does not work in these unusual roof setups.

phrases.english: As the school of Rav said in the name of Rav:
For example, where it was breached at a corner
and its roofing was slanted,
phrases.notes: A slanted roof cannot 'come down and seal.'

phrases.english: here too (for Shmuel),
for example, where it was breached at a corner
and its roofing is 'in four.'
phrases.notes: Sealing would have to work on all four sides, which שמואל does not accept (step 10).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised again in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא) to a corner breach
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is about a normal house, where the roof edge should seal two sides.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is about a corner breach with an unusual roof, where פי תקרה does not work.

steps.title: Why שמואל did not use רב's explanation
steps.stepSummary: שמואל did not explain the משנה as a slanted roof, because the משנה never says 'slanted.'
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל did not explain it like רב, because the משנה does not say 'slanted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why שמואל chose his own explanation instead of רב's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's whole answer depends on the roof being slanted. The משנה never mentions that detail, so שמואל did not want to add it.

phrases.english: Shmuel did not say like Rav,
(because) 'slanted' is not taught (in the Mishnah).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the two explanations in step 12 differ, starting with שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה does not mention a slanted roof.

steps.title: Why רב did not use שמואל's explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב could not use שמואל's case. That case would be like an אכסדרה, and רב holds that one may carry throughout an אכסדרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב did not explain it like שמואל, because if so, it would be an אכסדרה. And רב follows his own reasoning, for he said: in an אכסדרה, it is permitted to carry in the whole thing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב did not accept שמואל's explanation. It says the reason fits a view רב holds elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שמואל's case, the roof edge would have to seal all four sides. That is just like an אכסדרה, a roofed porch with no real walls. רב holds that פי תקרה works even there, so carrying is allowed. That means שמואל's case would not be forbidden for רב, and so it cannot explain the משנה's prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: a roofed porch or portico without real walls

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the real difference between רב and שמואל is whether פי תקרה can seal all four sides.

phrases.english: And Rav did not say like Shmuel,
because if so, it would be a portico,
and Rav follows his reasoning, for he said:
in a portico it is permitted to carry throughout.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes explaining the difference between the two explanations, now from רב's side.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: For רב, sealing all four sides works (אכסדרה), so שמואל's case would not be forbidden.

steps.title: The source: the dispute about an אכסדרה in a valley
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the original מחלוקת. רב permits carrying in the whole אכסדרה in a valley. שמואל permits carrying only within four אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was stated: an אכסדרה in a valley. רב said: it is permitted to carry in all of it. And שמואל said: one may carry in it only within four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source showing that רב really holds what was just said about an אכסדרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב treats the roof edge as walls on all four sides, so the whole porch counts as an enclosed area. שמואל does not accept sealing on all four sides, so the porch is like the open field around it. There, one may carry only within four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was stated (quoting an earlier dispute)

steps.whatToRemember: רב: פי תקרה works even for all four sides (אכסדרה is permitted). שמואל: it works for up to three sides, but not all four. This is why each explains the משנה about a breached house differently.

phrases.english: As it was stated: a portico in a valley.
Rav said: it is permitted to carry in all of it.
And Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מְטַלְטְלִין בָּהּ אֶלָּא בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת.
phrases.english: one may not carry in it except within four cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for 'רב follows his reasoning' in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רב's view that one may carry throughout an אכסדרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The recorded מחלוקת of רב and שמואל about an אכסדרה in a valley

steps.title: The reasons behind רב and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רב permits carrying in the whole אכסדרה because he holds פי תקרה יורד וסותם. שמואל permits only four אמות because he does not hold that rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב said: You may carry in the whole porch, because we say that the edge of the roof comes down and closes it off. שמואל said: You may carry there only within four אמות, because we do not say that the edge of the roof comes down and closes it off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the מחלוקת it just quoted, but this time it adds the reason behind each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The whole argument depends on one idea: פי תקרה יורד וסותם, that the edge of a roof is treated as if it drops down and forms a wall. רב accepts this, so the porch counts as walled in on all sides and you may carry throughout. שמואל rejects it, so the open porch is not enclosed and you may carry only within four אמות.

keyTerms.meaning: A porch or portico: a roof resting on posts, with open sides
The edge of the roof is treated as if it comes down and seals the side like a wall
Four cubits, the small area in which one may carry even without walls
To carry or move objects on שבת

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why the גמרא in step 14 said רב could not use שמואל's case. For רב, such a case is like an אכסדרה, and the roof edge would seal it.

phrases.english: Rav said: It is permitted to carry in all of it,
because we say: the edge of the roof descends and seals.
And Shmuel said: One may not carry in it
except within four cubits,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָמְרִינַן פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם.
phrases.english: because we do not say: the edge of the roof descends and seals.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָמַר: מוּתָּר לְטַלְטֵל בְּכוּלָּהּ, אָמְרִינַן פִּי תִקְרָה יוֹרֵד וְסוֹתֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the מחלוקת quoted in step 15 and adds the reason behind each opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב holds פי תקרה יורד וסותם, so carrying is permitted in the whole אכסדרה. שמואל rejects it, so carrying is limited to four אמות.

steps.title: First version: they argue only about openings wider than ten
steps.stepSummary: If the openings are ten אמות or less, everyone agrees carrying is permitted. They argue only when the openings are wider than ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the openings are ten אמות, everyone agrees. Where they argue is when the openings are more than ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא narrows down exactly which case רב and שמואל are arguing about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An opening of up to ten אמות can be treated as a doorway (פתח), not a breach. So in that case nobody needs the roof-edge rule, and all agree you may carry. The roof-edge idea only matters for openings wider than ten, and that is where רב and שמואל argue.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; there is no argument here

phrases.english: With ten: everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: Openings of up to ten count as doorways, so carrying is allowed.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is with more than ten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the exact case in which the מחלוקת from step 16 applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At ten אמות or less, carrying is permitted according to all. The מחלוקת is only about openings wider than ten.

steps.title: Second version: they argue only about openings of ten
steps.stepSummary: Some say the opposite. If the openings are wider than ten, everyone agrees carrying is forbidden. The argument is about openings of ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: If the openings are more than ten, everyone agrees. Where they argue is when the openings are ten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the case, which flips the first one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, the roof-edge rule cannot seal openings wider than ten, so everyone agrees carrying is forbidden there. The argument moves to openings of ten or less. רב says the roof edge seals them. שמואל says it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say: this introduces another version of the same teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The two versions do not just differ in detail; they are opposites. In the first version, ten is clearly permitted and wider than ten is argued about. In the second version, wider than ten is clearly forbidden and ten is argued about.
steps.whatToRemember: רב permits carrying in an אכסדרה based on פי תקרה יורד וסותם, and שמואל rejects that rule. There are two versions of where they argue. One version says wider than ten, with ten agreed as permitted. The other says ten, with wider than ten agreed as forbidden.

phrases.english: And some say:
With more than ten: everyone agrees.
phrases.notes: Here, everyone agrees carrying is forbidden.

phrases.english: Where they disagree is with ten.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, בְּיָתֵר — כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative version that reverses the case definition in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Openings wider than ten are forbidden according to all. The מחלוקת is only about openings of ten.

steps.title: Introducing a statement of רב יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to bring a teaching of רב יהודה, which it will connect to the two versions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that which רב יהודה said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is about to quote רב יהודה, and the quote itself continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'והא דאמר' signal that the גמרא will bring a known statement and fit it into the discussion. Most likely it will show which version of the מחלוקת that statement follows. The actual content has not been given yet.

keyTerms.meaning: And that which [someone] said: this introduces a known statement to be connected to the discussion
An אמורא, a student of רב and שמואל

phrases.english: And that which Rav Yehuda said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets up a statement that will be linked to the two versions in steps 17 and 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not stated yet; the content of רב יהודה's statement continues on the next amud.
